validity.recommendation: Do not treat the specs as sourced. Find an independent, pipeline-specific source (Iraqi Oil Ministry / North Gas Company / SOMO, or Arabic Kirkuk press) that names a North Gas Company gas line to K1 and gives length/diameter/capacity before leaving this as a fully-attributed operating row; otherwise flag the whole row (esp. Capacity) as unverified. If none surfaces, consider whether this is a phantom/relabel of the broader NGC Kirkuk gas network rather than a discrete 34 km trunk.
validity.researcher_notes: SOLE SUPPORT IS AN AGGREGATE, NON-NAMING, DEAD CITATION. The gem.wiki page's only outbound reference is 'OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012, p.75' at opec.org/.../ASB2012.pdf. That URL no longer resolves to the PDF (now returns an HTML redirect/404 page, not a document), so it cannot be verified, and the ASB is an aggregate statistical bulletin that does not itself define a discrete pipeline named 'North Gas-K1' with these attributes -- the pipeline name and all specs (34 km, 18 in, 5.26 bcm/y) are a GEM construction from that table. Per the sweep rule, a row whose only support is a generic/aggregate citation that does not name the pipeline is itself an existence flag. NO INDEPENDENT SOURCE NAMES THIS SPECIFIC LINE. I searched English and Arabic (INA/SOMO/oil-ministry, Kirkuk press). What IS independently confirmed is only the surrounding context, not P2232: (a) K1 is a real pump-station hub at Kirkuk (iraqinews, verified); (b) North Gas Company (NGC) operates a gas-transmission network in the Kirkuk area feeding power stations -- the June-2025 corrosion blast ~55 km WEST of Kirkuk hit an NGC domestic gas pipeline carrying Kirkuk-field gas to power stations at Baiji (shafaq EN, kurdistan24, verified). But that Baiji-directed line corresponds to roster sibling P2231 (North Gas-Baiji, 145 km), not to a 34 km North Gas->K1 line. So the NGC Kirkuk gas network exists, but a discrete '34 km / 18 in / 5.26 bcm/y' North Gas->K1 trunk has zero pipeline-specific corroboration. SPEC RED FLAG reinforcing the concern: 5.26 bcm/y is ~510 MMscf/d, implausibly high for an 18-inch, 34 km line (18-inch domestic trunks in this same country run ~100 MMscf/d, cf. roster P6827/P7477); and the sibling OPEC-derived rows show mutually incoherent 'bcm/y' magnitudes (P2231=0.89, P2232=5.26, P2233=150.00) -- a signature of a units/transcription artifact in the source table, so the capacity in particular should not be trusted. CLASSIFICATION: gas classification is defensible ('North Gas' = NGC, a gas operator; K1 = Kirkuk; not one of the GulfPub Iraq crude/NGL lines). DUPLICATE: not an obvious duplicate of another roster row -- distinct from P2231 (Baiji), P2233 (Taji, 438 km), and P6827 (Khormor-Jambur-Kirkuk, 1.05 km branch to Kirkuk power station); but it could be a relabel/segment of the same NGC Kirkuk feeder network, which the existence work above could not rule in or out. Net: real physical NGC gas infrastructure almost certainly exists in this corridor, but THIS row as a discrete, spec'd entity is unverified on every attribute.

routes.start_name: North Gas Company gas facility, Kirkuk group fields (unsourced exact location)
routes.corridor_desc: Corridor lies within Kirkuk (Saladin-adjacent) governorate in northern Iraq. The named end, K1, is the well-known pump-station hub at Kirkuk (~35.47N, 44.39E; anchored to Kirkuk city, approximate). The 'North Gas' start is the North Gas Company gas plant/gathering point serving the Kirkuk group of fields (Baba/Avana domes, Jambur, Bai Hassan, Khabbaz) south/southeast of Kirkuk; a ~34 km length is consistent with a line from the Jambur/Bai Hassan area (~35.1-35.2N, 44.4-44.6E) north to K1 at Kirkuk, but I could not source the exact plant coordinate, so the start lat/lon are left null. Bound is LOOSE: both endpoints sit inside a roughly 40 km radius of Kirkuk city, so the corridor is confidently within Kirkuk governorate but the precise alignment is unestablished.
routes.researcher_notes: End (K1) established as a Kirkuk facility from iraqinews (verified 200, mentions K1 + Kirkuk); coordinate anchored to Kirkuk city (real, well-known place), flagged approximate. Start (NGC gas facility) named from independent context (NGC operates the Kirkuk-field gas network per shafaq/kurdistan24) but its precise coordinate is NOT sourced, so start_lat/start_lon left null rather than fabricated. No coordinate was invented; the two-day-inspection blast reports place NGC gas lines in this exact Kirkuk corridor, supporting the corridor but not a precise route.

summary: P2232 CONCERN (existence): named 'North Gas-K1' line and all specs rest solely on an aggregate, non-naming, now-dead OPEC ASB 2012 citation; no independent source names the line or confirms 34 km/18 in/5.26 bcm/y (capacity implausibly high for 18-in), though NGC's Kirkuk gas network is real; route suggested at LOW (K1=Kirkuk anchored, NGC-plant start coords unsourced/null).
